text:
incident-bot: 🚨 URGENT: Runtime alarms - canary GPU pool 7 showing elevated tail latency and error spike (link: https://monitoring.redwood/alarms/1749001234)
oncall-sam: paging — I'm awake, looking. starting triage.
maria: seeing p50 stable but p95->p99 jumps on canary-7 around 1749001100. graphs show repeated kernel fallback events + microbatch queue growth.
raj: can you paste the kernel logs? I want to see fallback reasons.
maria: log snippet:```
2026-03-17T03:05:10Z runtime: kernel_select: fallback to generic_kernel.cu (latency=12.4ms)
2026-03-17T03:05:10Z runtime: kvcache_miss spike, batch_size unexpectedly small -> repeated kernel swaps
2026-03-17T03:06:01Z batcher: enqueue_wait > 150ms, prefetch stall
```
ops-jen: that matches the canary deploy from 1748999000 (quantized route selector change).
oncall-sam: rollback option? we can flip ff for the selector or cut traffic to canary pool. Which is faster?
eng-ryan: killing the selector flag is fastest. ff name is rollout/quant-route-v2. Command: `/ff disable rollout/quant-route-v2 --env=canary`
raj: if we disable the flag, will requests go to a prior kernel path or a different model variant? need to confirm no other regressions.
maria: disabling will route to legacy kernel selector (pre-quant route). it should stop the thrash. still want to cut traffic if ff disable doesn't converge quickly.
oncall-sam: doing it now — `/ff disable rollout/quant-route-v2 --env=canary`
incident-bot: action logged: feature flag rollout/quant-route-v2 disabled by oncall-sam at 1749001320
maria: within 30s p99 fell from 420ms -> 160ms on canary-7. queueing normalized. good sign.
support-ben: any customer impact? I have two enterprise customers pinging support about longer inference times.
pm-clara: I'll draft a short note for affected customers: "We briefly observed elevated latency in our canary pool after a targeted rollout; mitigation in progress. No data exposure. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."
ops-jen: hold on — seeing a second symptom: batching throughput dropped ~25% for requests with variable seq_len. metric: tokens/sec per GPU decreased. might be related to kernel code path still active for some sessions.
eng-ryan: some sessions may have pinned kernels in the KV cache / session affinity. need to evict sessions on canary-7 to force re-resolve. Command: `curl -X POST https://ops.redwood/evict-sessions -d '{"pool":"canary-7","age_gt":"2m"}'`
oncall-sam: running evict now.
incident-bot: evict-sessions job started (job_id: evict-1749001500)
maria: after evict, throughput recovered to ~95% baseline; p99 stable. looks like combined effect: selector change + long-lived sessions pinned the fallback kernel.
raj: recommend full rollback of rollout/quant-route-v2 in prod until we have tests for session-pinning interactions.
eng-ryan: agreed. I'll open a PR to revert the selector change and add an integration test simulating pinned kvcache sessions.
support-ben: sending customer update: "Mitigation applied, most traffic restored. We'll post a follow-up postmortem with timeline and mitigation steps"
pm-clara: flagging for postmortem and severity assessment. Suspect moderate customer impact for a small subset of customers using long chat sessions.
oncall-sam: handing off to eng-ryan for next steps and postmortem. I'll remain on channel for 30m in case issues resurface. :thumbsup:
eng-ryan: taking ownership for RCA and the rollback PR. I'll coordinate with QA for the session-affinity test.
incident-bot: incident updated: status=mitigated, lead=eng-ryan, mitigations=[ff_disable, session_evict], start_ts=1749001100, mitigated_ts=1749001420
pm-clara: created support ticket bundle and customer comms draft (link: https://support.redwood/ticket/INC-1749001234)
support-ben: will follow up with affected customers and escalate to account teams as needed.
oncall-sam: closing pager for now, will reopen if any alarms reappear.
eng-ryan: timeline + initial notes saved to /incidents/1749001234/correspondence.md. will author full postmortem tomorrow.
maria: leaving final note — watch for kernels selector metrics after rollback, especially batcher enqueue latencies.
incident-bot: incident closed (auto) at 1749004834 — please add tags [canary, rollback, kernel-selector, session-affinity] to postmortem.
